## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the change does what the description says, and the kernel source supports `i915.enable_dpcd_backlight=3` specifically. One robustness gap was found in the migration's retry behavior. Its impact is low and it resolves at the next boot-image rebuild.

| Question | Result |
|---|---|
| Driver | In linux-omarchy 7.2.5, xe still requires `force_probe` for Meteor Lake and the shipped config leaves it empty, so i915 binds the iGPU. The `i915.` prefix is correct. |
| Value `3` | The "missing HDR static metadata" message quoted in the PR is printed only after the panel passes the Intel TCON and NITS capability checks (`intel_dp_aux_backlight.c`). Value 3 (force Intel) is the only value that skips the HDR metadata check, so `=1` would still reject the interface. |
| Fallback | A panel without the Intel interface returns `-ENODEV` and falls back to PWM (`intel_backlight.c`), which is the current behavior. |
| Range | With no HDR metadata the driver uses a default 0..512 range, which matches the reported `max_brightness` of 512. |
| Hardware match | `omarchy-hw-match` greps the DMI product name case-insensitively. The public GU605MY DMI product name is `ROG Zephyrus G16 GU605MY_GU605MY`. The real matcher logic, run against synthetic DMI strings, matches GU605MY and rejects GU605MV/MI/MZ/MU, GU605CW and GU604VY. |
| Drop-in | limine-entry-tool (1.38.0 and 1.39.0) reads `/etc/limine-entry-tool.d/*.conf` and treats `KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=` as an addition to the default cmdline. The format matches the existing Panther Lake drop-in. |
| New installs | The omarchy-iso installer runs hardware setup, then `limine-update`, so the first boot image carries the option. |
| Migration guards | No-op on other hardware, without `limine-mkinitcpio`, and when the drop-in already exists. |
| Test | The new test passes on the PR head and fails on the base tree. |

### Migration does not retry a failed rebuild

`migrations/1790188786.sh` uses the drop-in's existence as its only completion guard, but it writes the drop-in before rebuilding. If the rebuild does not complete, a later run sees the file and exits successfully without rebuilding or requesting a reboot:

```text
run 1: no drop-in -> write drop-in -> limine-mkinitcpio fails (e.g. Ctrl-C, ESP not mounted)
       -> migration exits non-zero, stays pending            (correct)
run 2: drop-in exists -> guard false -> exit 0, no rebuild, no reboot flag
       -> omarchy-migrate marks it complete                  (option not in boot image)
```

This sequence was reproduced with a stubbed failing `limine-mkinitcpio` in an isolated fixture. Separately, `limine-mkinitcpio` itself exits 0 when a per-kernel image build or the copy to the ESP fails (`limine-mkinitcpio-install` swallows those errors). In that case the first run also completes without the option in the boot image. `migrations/1789325478.sh` notes this upstream behavior for the same reason.

**Impact:** on an affected GU605MY, brightness keys stay non-functional and no reboot is requested until the next successful rebuild. The limine-mkinitcpio pacman hook triggers one on the next kernel, firmware, systemd or mkinitcpio update. The machine keeps booting the previous image throughout.

**Suggested change:** guard on a machine-wide marker such as `/var/lib/omarchy/migrations/1790188786`, written only after `sudo limine-mkinitcpio` succeeds, as `migrations/1786482992.sh` and `migrations/1785944594.sh` do. That retries interrupted and ESP-not-mounted rebuilds. The zero-exit case would need a check of the built image; the menu-entry check in `1789325478.sh` does not transfer here because the entries already exist.

**Optional test improvement:** no test case runs without `limine-mkinitcpio`. Removing the migration's `omarchy-cmd-present limine-mkinitcpio` guard still passes the test (the only surviving mutant of eight single-edit mutants). A case with the stub absent would cover it.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the PR, Linux 7.2.5 i915/xe display code, limine-entry-tool 1.38.0 and 1.39.0, and the omarchy-iso installer order. The PR's test, `bash -n`, eight single-edit mutants and stubbed migration scenarios (synthetic DMI strings, no Limine, failed then retried rebuild) ran in an isolated sandbox. Not tested on GU605MY hardware: panel brightness at 512, suspend/resume and MUX-mode behavior rest on the PR author's report. The `./test/cli` baseline claim was not checked.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with targeted follow-up questions, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
